newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Amoco mulls oil and gas projects in Romania.
newsitem.headline: Amoco mulls oil and gas projects in Romania.

text.p: The Romanian subsidiary of Amoco Corp said on Wednesday it was interested in oil and gas projects in Romania but denied local media reports saying it would invest $1 billion.

Michael Adams, president of Amoco Romania Petroleum Co told Reuters the company had discussed with Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea earlier in the day projects to increase gas and oil production on twenty oil and gas fields across the country.

Under the proposal, Amoco would cooperate with the local Petrom RA oil exploration company and Romgaz RA gas utility to upgrade the 20 oil and deposits over the next 10 years. The project would allow Romania to cut energy imports, he said.
"It is premature to say now the final figure for the investment. It is true that the investment might be significant but it will highly depend on the outcome of the negotiations," Adams said.
It was a reference to local media reports saying Amoco would invest one billion dollars in the Balkan country.
Government officials were unavailable for comment.
Adams said Amoco had also asked Ciorbea to consider several amendments to a petroleum law, passed by parliament last year.
The bill, which Western oil operators in Romania said was "workable" puts local and foreign oil operators on equal footiong and grants incentives to strategic investors.
"The amendements suggested by us involve things that are standar in other areas of the world for petroleum operations and they could strenghten Romania's legislation," Adams said.
Ciorbea had promised to give an answer to Amoco's projects and demands within a month, Adams said.
"We are not asking for special incentives for Amoco," Adams said without elaborating.
